summary: Siemens S7COMM is a proprietary PLC control protocol carried over ISO 8073 Class 0 (COTP) framed with RFC 1006 (ISO Transport over TCP), commonly on 102/tcp. An attacker who reaches port 102 typically gets unauthenticated read of PLC identity, code blocks (DB/M/I/Q memory) when the CPU has legacy PUT/GET enabled, and — on S7-300/400 or misconfigured 1200/1500 — the ability to STOP/START the CPU, upload/download OB/DB blocks, and read out the CPU protection password or bypass it. The high-value target is unambiguous OT-on-IT segmentation evidence plus a firmware/order-code fingerprint that maps to a large body of Siemens PLC CVEs (CVE-2015-2177, CVE-2020-15782, CVE-2022-38465, URGENT/11). Recce currently only labels the port in svcdetect; there is no probe module, no serviceenum mapping, and no per-service script. A modbus.py-shaped module using stdlib socket+struct can add high-signal OT findings without any writes to the device.
default_ports: 44818/tcp (not S7 — do not confuse with EtherNet/IP)

existing_coverage.notes: svcdetect labels port 102 correctly, but there is NO recce/services/s7.py probe module, NO entry in recce/services/serviceenum.py _PORT/_NAME maps (so `recce services` prints nothing for open 102), and NO recce/scripts/recce-service-s7.sh. `is_s7()` predicate does not exist. TPKT parsing exists in rdp.py (RDP shares the RFC 1006 framing) and can be borrowed for the COTP/TPKT layer.

capabilities.name: cotp_connect_probe
capabilities.description: Send a COTP Connection Request (X.224 CR, TPDU code 0xE0) inside a TPKT (RFC 1006) and confirm a Connection Confirm (0xD0) comes back — distinguishes a real ISO-on-TCP stack from arbitrary listeners on 102/tcp.
capabilities.notes: Two-byte length in TPKT is big-endian; identical framing to RDP's _X224_CR in rdp.py — reuse that skeleton.

capabilities.name: tsap_rack_slot_enum
capabilities.description: Iterate common destination TSAPs (0x0102=rack0/slot2 CPU, 0x0201, 0x0202, 0x0300, 0x1000 OP) with source 0x0100 PG until COTP CC succeeds, revealing which rack/slot the CPU lives at and confirming PLC family.
capabilities.protocol_reference: Siemens S7 addressing: TSAP high-byte = comm type (1=PG, 2=OP, 3=S7-Basic), low-byte = (rack<<5)|slot
capabilities.notes: Also enumerates non-CPU modules — CPs (comm processors) answer on their own slots.

capabilities.name: s7_setup_communication
capabilities.description: After COTP CC, send an S7 ROSCTR=1 Job with function 0xF0 (Setup Communication) negotiating PDU size — a valid Ack_Data (ROSCTR=3) with function 0xF0 proves the S7 protocol stack, not just ISO-TSAP.
capabilities.protocol_reference: S7COMM (Wireshark dissector packet-s7comm.c) ROSCTR types 0x01 Job / 0x03 Ack_Data; function 0xF0

capabilities.name: szl_module_identification
capabilities.description: Userdata request (ROSCTR=7) function 0x11 (READ_SZL) with SZL-ID 0x0011 index 0x0001 returns the CPU order code (MLFB, e.g. '6ES7 315-2EH14-0AB0'), hardware version, and firmware version — the crown-jewel fingerprint for CVE mapping.
capabilities.protocol_reference: Siemens S7-300/400 System Software Reference Manual, SZL-ID 0x0011 (Modulkennung)
capabilities.notes: Order code prefix disambiguates S7-300 (6ES7 3xx), S7-400 (6ES7 4xx), S7-1200 (6ES7 2xx), S7-1500 (6ES7 5xx). Feeds firmware_cve_fingerprint.

capabilities.name: szl_component_identification
capabilities.description: SZL-ID 0x001C returns component-identification strings: PLC name (index 1), module name (2), plant designation (3), copyright (4), serial number (5), module-type name (6), OEM ID (7), location designation (8) — free text set by the engineer, often naming the process or site.
capabilities.notes: 'Plant designation' and 'location designation' are goldmine strings — feed known_hostnames + a new known_ot_assets surface.

capabilities.name: szl_cpu_protection_level
capabilities.description: SZL-ID 0x0232 index 0x0004 reports CPU protection level (1=none, 2=write-protect, 3=read+write-protect) and whether a password is set — indicates whether legacy password auth is required for privileged S7COMM operations.
capabilities.protocol_reference: Siemens S7-300 CPU Manual §Protection Level; SZL 0x0232 (Schutzstufe)

capabilities.name: szl_communication_capabilities
capabilities.description: SZL-IDs 0x0131/0x0132 expose whether PUT/GET communication is enabled — when on (default on S7-300/400, explicit opt-in on 1200/1500), any client that can reach 102/tcp can read and WRITE DB/M/I/Q memory without authentication.
capabilities.protocol_reference: Siemens Security Guideline for SIMATIC S7-1200/1500 §PUT/GET; SZL 0x0131

capabilities.name: s7_read_var_memory
capabilities.description: Function 0x04 (Read Variable) against a small, safe address (e.g. one byte of M0.0) proves unauthenticated read of process image / data blocks is possible — direct evidence PUT/GET is exploitable, no writes required.
capabilities.protocol_reference: S7COMM function 0x04 (Read Var), area codes 0x81 I / 0x82 Q / 0x83 M / 0x84 DB
capabilities.notes: Read-only. Keep to a single byte at a well-defined address; some CPUs raise access-denied on M0 if protection level 3.

capabilities.name: cpu_stop_start_control
capabilities.description: S7COMM function 0x29 (PLC STOP) and 0x28 (PLC START/HOT/COLD RESTART) halt or reboot the CPU, dropping the physical process — do NOT invoke from the probe; emit as an exploit runbook step gated behind operator confirmation.
capabilities.protocol_reference: S7COMM ROSCTR=1 function 0x29 (PLC STOP) with 'P_PROGRAM' parameter; CVE-2015-2177

capabilities.name: legacy_cpu_password_bypass
capabilities.description: S7-300/400 CPU protection passwords are transmitted as 8-byte SIMATIC 'obfuscated' blocks (XOR against 0x55 with a byte-rotation) that are offline-crackable and, for firmware <=CVE-2016-9159, retrievable via SZL 0x0132 index 0x0003 without authentication.
capabilities.protocol_reference: CVE-2016-9159; SCADACS Plcinject/snap7 reference; Siemens Advisory SSA-731239

capabilities.name: s7_1500_plus_detect
capabilities.description: S7-1200 firmware v4+ and S7-1500 speak S7COMM-PLUS (opcode 0x72) with TLS-wrapped session establishment — detect the 0x72 opcode in the response and flag that legacy S7COMM attacks (PUT/GET, STOP) do not apply, but the CPU may still expose CVE-2020-15782 memory-write.
capabilities.protocol_reference: Wireshark dissector packet-s7comm-plus.c; Siemens Advisory SSA-434534 (CVE-2020-15782)

capabilities.name: firmware_cve_fingerprint
capabilities.description: Cross-reference the order code + firmware version from szl_module_identification against a bundled Siemens PLC CVE table (URGENT/11 on VxWorks-based CPs, SSA-434534, SSA-731239, SSA-731239 password readout, CVE-2022-38465 hard-coded key) and emit per-CVE findings.

capabilities.name: block_list_enumeration
capabilities.description: Userdata function 0x11 sub-function 0x0d (List Blocks / List Blocks of Type) enumerates OB / FB / FC / DB / SDB block numbers present on the CPU — reveals program structure, custom function blocks, and the DB numbers worth reading with s7_read_var_memory.

capabilities.name: s7_segmentation_finding
capabilities.description: Emit a HIGH segmentation finding whenever a reachable S7 CPU is on a non-OT segment (mirrors modbus_reachable's stance) — OT PLCs on corporate/DMZ segments are a compliance and safety issue regardless of what else the probe learns.
capabilities.protocol_reference: IEC 62443-3-3 SR 5.1 Network Segmentation; NIST SP 800-82r3 §5.5

cross_service_wire_candidates: PLC name + module name + plant designation + location designation (SZL 0x001C indices 1,2,3,8) → known_hostnames (engineer-set free text often names the site/process/cell)
CPU order code MLFB (e.g. '6ES7 315-2EH14-0AB0') → NEW shared surface known_ot_assets (order_code, firmware, serial) so other services (modbus, EtherNet/IP later) can cluster PLCs by asset identity
CPU serial number (SZL 0x001C index 5) → NEW shared surface known_serials for cross-report asset tracking and crown-jewels tagging
Firmware version → feeds a new firmware_versions surface consumed by a future cve_matcher pass (aligns with Modbus vendor/product cross-ref)
Legacy CPU password recovered via legacy_cpu_password_bypass → known_hashes / a new known_ot_passwords surface (S7 password reuse across engineering-station/HMI accounts is common)
Rack/slot topology from tsap_rack_slot_enum → host.notes or a new known_ot_topology surface — informs which slot future writes/reads would target
OEM ID string (SZL 0x001C index 7) → known_domains (OEM integrators often stamp their company name here, revealing the third-party who commissioned the plant)

recommended_findings.title: Siemens S7 PLC reachable on scanned network
S7 CPU identity disclosed (order code + firmware)
S7 PUT/GET communication enabled — unauthenticated memory read/write
S7 unauthenticated variable read succeeded (M/DB memory)
S7 CPU STOP/START function reachable — process DoS possible
S7COMM-PLUS (S7-1200 v4 / S7-1500) detected — legacy attacks not applicable
S7 firmware matches published Siemens advisory (per-CVE)
S7 block list enumerated (OB/FB/FC/DB inventory disclosed)

recommended_hashcat_modes.description: Telegram (placeholder — no core hashcat mode exists for S7 legacy 8-byte SIMATIC obfuscation; recovered password is plaintext after XOR/rotate deobfuscation, not a hash, so no hashcat step is needed — document in the finding rather than emit a crack task)

implementation_notes: Model the module on recce/services/modbus.py — stdlib socket+struct only, single ~4s connect, read-only, findings emphasize OT-on-IT segmentation stance. Reuse the TPKT framing pattern from recce/services/rdp.py (RFC 1006 is identical between RDP and S7 at the transport layer). Add is_s7(port) predicate matching port 102 or service names containing 'iso-tsap' / 's7' / 'siemens'. Register 102 → 's7' in recce/services/serviceenum.py _PORT and 'iso-tsap' → 's7' in _NAME, and add a recce/scripts/recce-service-s7.sh driver so `recce services` emits it. Wire in via recce/services/__init__.py and the analyze() dispatcher (mirror modbus.analyze signature). NEVER emit function 0x05 (Write Var), 0x28/0x29 (START/STOP), or 0x1A/0x1B/0x1C (block upload/download/insert) from the probe — those go in the runbook as manual exploit steps behind explicit operator confirmation, per the airgap constraint's read-only stance. TSAP enumeration loop should cap at ~6 attempts to keep budget within svcprobe.iter_probe defaults. Also add S7 to any OT-segmentation cross-service aggregator that currently only reads modbus (grep for modbus_reachable in recce/core/attackpath/ if that consumer exists).
